# Kar-Warden

> An integrity gate for AI components, with no LLM judge. Declare a component's warrant (baseline config
> hash, allowed capabilities, required files, named invariants); present its observed state; get a
> deterministic, re-runnable verdict — INTACT, DRIFTED or BREACHED — naming exactly what broke. Runs
> entirely client-side.

## What it is
- A pure, gate-proven kernel + a single-file page that inlines it. No backend, no data leaves the browser.
- One severe break (changed config, ungranted capability, missing file, failed severe invariant) is a
  BREACH and cannot be averaged away by passing checks.

## Core functions
- verifyIntegrity(warrant, observed) -> verdict { status, broken[], brokenCount, severeCount }
- monitorStatus(warrants[], observations[]) -> StatusReport (worst status wins; missing = UNREPORTED)
- appendAnomaly(chain, entry) / verifyChain(chain) -> hash-chained tamper-evident log
- wardenReceipt(...) / verifyWardenReceipt(r) -> portable receipt a third party re-runs to reproduce the verdict

## Proof
- Mutation gate (witness): 72/73 killed, score 0.986, 1 reviewed-equivalent.
- The live page is generated from the kernel and diff-checked in CI, so it cannot drift from the proven code.
